what: General term for members of Vishnuite orders; formerly mendicants, now a caste; Kabirpanthi/Satnami etc. not generally called Bairagi
quote: Properly, a religious mendicant of any Vishnuite sect should be called a Bairagi.

what: Four Sampradayas (Ramanuji, Ramanandi, Nimanandi, Madhavachari/Vallabhacharya per list of paragraphs) and minor sects
quote: It is generally held that there are four Sampradayas or main orders.

what: Seven Akharas (Digambari, Khaki, Munjia, Kathia, Nirmohi, Nirbani, Lasgari) instituted as military divisions when the Bairagis had to fight the Gosains; Naga members fought; meet once in 12 years
quote: instituted when the Bairagis had to fight with the Gosains.

what: Quarrels with Gosains at sacred rivers over which sect should bathe first
quote: The quarrels between the Bairagis and Gosains usually occurred at the sacred rivers, and the point of contention was which sect should bathe first.

what: Social position fairly good; act as gurus to laymen of all castes; Ram/Gopal mantra to twice-born, Sheo mantra to others; property of unmarried Bairagi goes to chela
quote: They act as gurus or spiritual guides to the laymen of all castes who can become Bairagis.

what: Maths: huts for Mahant and pupils, temple, samadhi, dharmsala; small land endowment; successor elected by Mahants of neighbouring maths if unmarried
quote: The Bairagis have numerous maths or monasteries, scattered over the country and usually attached to temples.

what: Married Bairagis form an ordinary caste; many acquired property (text continues)
quote: Large numbers of Bairagis now marry and have children, and have formed an ordinary caste.
